0.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in the presence of or in front of the king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of] or [in front of]

The pronoun in **he sent him** refers to Abimelech, while the pronouns in **him away** and **he left** refer to David. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the king sent David away and David left]

1.q: אֲבָרֲכָ֣ה אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּ⁠כָל־עֵ֑ת תָּ֝מִ֗יד תְּֽהִלָּת֥⁠וֹ בְּ⁠פִֽ⁠י
1.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in the Psalms, and follow that approach here and throughout this psalm. Alternate translation: [I will praise Yahweh without ceasing] or [I will bless Yahweh at all times, indeed, continually his praise is in my mouth]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **praise**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [praising him with my mouth]

Here, **my mouth** represents David’s speech. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I shall praise him with my words]

2.note: Here, **my soul** represents David himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I will boast]

David is using the adjective **humble** as a noun to mean people who are humble. If your language would not use an adjective this way, you could translate it with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [those who are humble]

3.q: גַּדְּל֣וּ לַ⁠יהוָ֣ה אִתִּ֑⁠י וּ⁠נְרוֹמְמָ֖ה שְׁמ֣⁠וֹ יַחְדָּֽו
3.note: See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in the Psalms, and follow that approach here and throughout this psalm. Alternate translation: [Let us declare together that Yahweh is great]

Here David is speaking of praising Yahweh as if Yahweh were something that they could **Magnify** or make larger. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Everyone should join me in telling others about how great Yahweh is]

This is an imperative, but it communicates an exhortation rather than a command. David is encouraging the people to worship. If the imperative does not communicate an exhortation for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates an exhortation or invitation. Alternate translation: [and we should all exalt his name]

Here, **his name** represents Yahweh himself and his reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everything about him]

4.note: David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a lost object which could be **sought** and found. He means that the people should pray to Yahweh and desire to be in his presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I asked Yahweh for help]

David is using **answered me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “acted on my behalf” in response to a request. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he acted in my behalf]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fears**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the things I feared]

5.note: Here, **They** refers to those who seek Yahweh mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Those who seek Yahweh look]

David is using **look to him** as a common expression of the culture to mean to “trust in Yahweh and ask him for help.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They trust him to help them]

The psalmist is speaking of the joy and gladness those who trust Yahweh feel as if they were shining with **radiant** light. If it would be helpful for your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and are glad]

The expression **let their faces not have shame** was a common expression meaning that they would not be ashamed because of some public failure or discouraged. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly or state it positively as in the UST. Alternate translation: [they should never be put to shame]

6.note: David is using the adjective **afflicted** as a noun to mean a person who is afflicted. Here David is referring to himself. If your language would not use an adjective this way, you could translate it with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [I was the suffering person who]

David assumes that readers will know that **Yahweh heard** means he listened to his prayer and responded favorably to it. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh did what I asked]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **troubles**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the things that were troubling him]

7.note: David is speaking of the angel protecting God’s people as if the angel were an army **encamping** around them to protect them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The angel of Yahweh stands guard around those who fear him]

David is using the possessive form to describe an **angel** that is sent by Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The angel sent by Yahweh]

8.note: David is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of joy or blessing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, how happy is]

David is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the person who takes refuge]

David is speaking of trusting in Yahweh as if it were physically seeking shelter or **refuge** in a safe place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he puts his trust in him]

David is speaking of experiencing Yahweh’s goodness as if it were some kind of food one could **Taste** and **see**. He means that one can discover Yahweh’s goodness by personal trial and experience. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Try for yourself and discover that Yahweh is good]

9.note: David is using the adjective **holy** as a noun to mean people who belong to Yahweh and are set apart for him. If your language would not use an adjective this way, you could translate it with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [his people who are set apart for him]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **lack**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [there is provision]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **lack**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [going without anything they need]

10.note: This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **lack**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this as modeled in the UST.

11.note: Although the term **sons** is masculine, David is using the word in a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a phrase that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [children]

David is speaking of his listeners as if they were his **sons**. He means that they are his students whom he will instruct. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [students]

12.q: מִֽי־הָ֭⁠אִישׁ הֶ⁠חָפֵ֣ץ חַיִּ֑ים אֹהֵ֥ב יָ֝מִ֗ים לִ⁠רְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב
12.note: David is using the question form for emphasis. If you would not use the question form for that purpose in your language, you could translate this as a statement. Alternate translation: [If you want to live and enjoy a long time of seeing good, then do what follows.]

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [is the person]

13.q: נְצֹ֣ר לְשׁוֹנְ⁠ךָ֣ מֵ⁠רָ֑ע וּ֝⁠שְׂפָתֶ֗י⁠ךָ מִ⁠דַּבֵּ֥ר מִרְמָֽה
13.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Do not say anything that is evil or deceptive]

David is using one part of a person, their **tongue**, to mean all of them in the act of speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [yourself from speaking evil words]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You could supply these words from context if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [guard your lips from speaking deceit]

David is using one part of a person, their **lips**, to mean all of them in the act of speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and yourself from deceptive speech]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **evil** and **deceit**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [from saying evil things … deceitful things]

14.note: David is speaking of doing what is evil as if it were walking on a path that a person could stop doing or **Turn away from**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Refuse to do what is evil]

This is an imperative, but it communicates an exhortation rather than a command. The psalmist is exhorting his students to stay away from evil. If the imperative does not communicate an exhortation for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates an exhortation. Alternate translation: [You should turn away from evil]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **evil**, **good**, and **peace**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [from doing what is wrong and do what is right; strive to live at peace with others and pursue living peacefully]

The terms **seek** and **pursue** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [earnestly strive to live peacefully]

15.note: Here, **eyes** represent Yahweh’s attention and watchful care. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh watchfully cares for the righteous]

David is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean people who do what is right. If your language would not use an adjective this way, you could translate it with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [righteous people]

Here, **ears** represents Yahweh’s attentive responsiveness to prayer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he listens attentively to their cry]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **cry**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [them when they cry]

16.note: Here, **face of Yahweh** represents his active presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh sets himself against the doers of evil]

Here, **their remembrance** represents the lasting legacy or memory that people leave behind. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [so that no one on earth will remember them]

The psalmist is using **cut off** as a common expression of the culture to mean “destroy” or “remove.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to remove]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **evil** and **remembrance**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [what is wicked … any trace of them]

17.note: Here, **They** refers to the righteous people mentioned in verse 15. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the referent explicitly. Alternate translation: [Righteous people cry out]

David assumes that readers will know that **Yahweh hears** means he listens to their prayer and responds favorably to it. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh did what they asked]

18.note: Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s availability or willingness to help as if he were standing right beside or **near** to those who cry out to him for help. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will always give help]

David is using **broken of heart** as a common expression of his culture to mean “overwhelmed with grief.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to those who are overwhelmed with grief]

David is using **crushed of spirit** as a common expression of his culture to mean “in deep despair.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and those who have lost all hope]

19.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evils**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [trials can happen to the righteous]

David is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean a person who does what is right. If your language would not use an adjective this way, you could translate it with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [of the righteous person]

Here, **him** refers to the righteous and **them** refers to the evils they experience. David uses the singular **him** to refer to the righteous as a collective group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [but Yahweh delivers each one of the righteous from all of those troubles]

20.note: Here, **He** refers to Yahweh, and **his** refers to the righteous person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is guarding all of the righteous person’s bones]

David is using one part of the body, **his bones**, to mean the whole physical body of the righteous person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [his physical body]

The expression **is broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [nothing breaks any one of them]

21.note: David speaks of **Evil** as if it were a person who could kill **the wicked**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this meaning in a non-figurative way. Alternate translation: [The evil deeds of the wicked will destroy them]

David is using the adjectives **the wicked** and **the righteous** as nouns to mean people who are wicked and people who are righteous. If your language would not use adjectives this way, you could translate them with equivalent expressions. Alternate translation: [those who are wicked … those who are righteous]

22.note: David is using the term **soul** to mean the entire person from the perspective of his spiritual existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the lives of those who worship him]

David is speaking of trusting in Yahweh as if he were a physical location, a **refuge**, that could provide safety and protection. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [trusting in him for protection]
